summary: The dispatched object does not exist. The subject path hashes 856f7cd2 stably across twelve measurements, while both the dispatch message and the review prompt expect f161d878, and no file anywhere in the repository carries that digest. The path has never been committed, so there is no prior version holding those bytes either. The prompt itself did not move and both frozen prior subjects are unedited, so the failure is isolated to the turn-3 draft. I have not read the subject and have not reviewed it on the merits: the freeze digest is what establishes which bytes are under review, and with it unmatched there is no authorized object to review.

objections.location: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-093.turn3.draft.md, against the expected digest carried identically by the dispatch and by coordinator-decisions.D-093.turn3.review-prompt.md
objections.claim: The subject on disk is not the subject that was dispatched. The freeze precondition for this turn is unmet, so no review of these bytes can be recorded as the turn-3 review.
objections.why: Both the dispatch and the prompt state the expected digest as f161d8785e0dfa2495867457b4038f2f8e9dcb9906a6de1fffa9b13a920e6952. The file at that path hashes 856f7cd23ebb433acdbb3c069cbf7b04087380d4e1c246f6f0e02ade4faaba22, and I measured it twelve times — three at the outset, six more when the first result surprised me, and three at the close — with the same value every time, so this is not a transient or a tooling artifact. I then looked for the dispatched bytes rather than only reporting their absence: no file in docs/coop/artifacts carries that digest, a walk of 1300 files across the repository finds no match anywhere, and the path has no git history, so the intended bytes are not recoverable from a prior commit. That rules out the benign readings — this is not a stale dispatch message quoting an older good version, because the prompt written alongside the draft carries the same expected value, and it is not a mis-typed path, because the path resolves to a real turn-3 draft of the right name and size. Either the draft was rewritten after its digest was taken, or the digest was computed from bytes that were never written to this path. The instruction is explicit in both places — 'This subject is FROZEN. If it moves, OBJECT' — and the digest is the entire mechanism by which a reviewer and a coordinator agree on what is being reviewed. Every prior cycle in this series matched exactly on the first measurement, which is itself evidence that the discipline holds and that something specific went wrong here. I have therefore not read the subject. Reviewing unfrozen bytes would produce findings that could later be cited as the turn-3 review of an object nobody authorized, which is a worse outcome than the delay.
objections.repair: Re-measure the intended turn-3 draft and re-dispatch with the digest that the file actually carries, or restore the bytes that hash to f161d878… if they exist outside this repository. Turn 3 can then run against an established object.
objections.procedureNote: This objection is not on the merits and should not be recorded as a merits deadlock. D-000 clause 2 sends an entry to CONTESTED when three turns of substantive disagreement fail to converge; that is not what happened here. I reviewed turns 1 and 2, raised one MUST-FIX and one note, and consented at turn 2 after both were repaired — I have no outstanding disagreement with D-093's substance. The correct remedy is re-dispatch at a correct digest, after which this turn can proceed normally.

whatIVerified: The subject digest, twelve times: three measurements at the start, six more after the initial mismatch, and three at the close. Every one returned 856f7cd23ebb433acdbb3c069cbf7b04087380d4e1c246f6f0e02ade4faaba22. The file is stable during the review; it simply is not the dispatched object.

The mismatch is not a stale dispatch message. I read the review prompt, as instructed, and it carries the identical expected digest f161d878… on its own line 8, so the dispatch and the prompt agree with each other and disagree with the file. Had the prompt named 856f7cd2…, this would have been a transcription problem in the dispatch alone.

The dispatched bytes do not exist anywhere I can reach. No file in docs/coop/artifacts hashes to f161d878…, and a walk of 1300 files across the whole working tree, excluding .git and dependency directories, finds no match. The path has no git history at all, so there is no committed version to recover.
The prompt itself did not move: 592a36a0291d0e8f4e4e94c830aa1b0675640c223ab1a8125e5836c141092bb6 at the start and again at the close, six measurements in total.

The failure is isolated to the turn-3 draft. Both frozen prior subjects measure exactly what this cycle has pinned throughout — turn 1 at fd45e7d177dbab44d7edd6dcf994eb8b5c5f650f6bc4e1003ca3c5dbc27f3713 and turn 2 at 1e6a236bcfe4bf3d3795e19332a46f97c07da0022a4c1fd9a42aad7dcfcc7c71 — so the attack 'turn-1 or turn-2 subject edited' fails and nothing already consented to has been disturbed.

The subject file is untracked, 8418 bytes, mode -r--r--r--, with mtime 2026-08-14 17:10:22, in the same minute as the prompt. Read-only mode is consistent with a freeze applied after writing, which does not establish that the bytes written were the bytes measured.
I did not read the subject. I hashed it and inspected its metadata only, so nothing in this verdict is informed by its contents and no part of it can be cited as a review of them.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with one MUST-FIX, and the objection is about identity rather than content. The digest is the only thing that makes a frozen review meaningful: it is how the coordinator and I agree that the bytes I judged are the bytes that will be adopted. Here the file hashes 856f7cd2 and both the dispatch and the prompt expect f161d878, stably, twelve measurements apart. I went looking for the dispatched bytes before concluding anything — not in the artifacts directory, not anywhere in 1300 files across the repository, and not in git history, since the path was never committed. So the benign explanations are closed off: the prompt was written alongside the draft and carries the same wrong expectation, which rules out a stale dispatch quoting an older good version. I deliberately did not read the subject. Findings drawn from unfrozen bytes could later be cited as the turn-3 review of an object nobody authorized, and that is a worse failure than a delay. I want one thing recorded clearly for the coordinator: this is not a substantive deadlock and should not become CONTESTED. I consented at turn 2 once my MUST-FIX and my note were repaired, and I hold no outstanding disagreement with this entry. Re-dispatch at the digest the file actually carries and turn 3 can run properly.
